# **1\.  Introduction**

## **1.1 Purpose**

This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) defines the functional and non-functional requirements for OurBike, a peer-to-peer motorized two-wheeler rental web application. It is intended for use by the development team and course instructors. This document follows the IEEE Std 830-1998 standard.

## **1.2 Scope**

**Product name:** OurBike.

OurBike is a web-based platform that enables owners of motorcycles and scooters to list their vehicles for short-term rental during periods of non-use. For example, while the owner is in class or at work. Renters can browse available vehicles, send a booking request, and are billed by the hour. They can also give rides to other users of the app for less money than other ride sharing apps. The Owner sets an hourly rate and a wear-and-tear charge per hour; the total fare is calculated from the actual time used.

**The system will:** 

* Allow vehicle owners to list, configure, and activate their two-wheelers for rental

* Allow renters to browse available vehicles, send booking requests and accept requests to give rides to passenger

* Compute billing based on time used, hourly rate, and wear-and-tear charge

* Provide owners and renters with earnings tracking and booking management

* Support a rating system for renters

**The system will not (in this version):** 

* Process real financial transactions. Billing is tracked but payment is handled outside the platform

* Perform live GPS tracking or automatic odometer reading

* Include distance-based or fuel-based billing

* Provide a native mobile application. All functionality is browser-based

* Include an administrator moderation panel

## **1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations**

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| Owner | A registered user who lists one or more vehicles for rental. |
| Renter | A registered user who browses and books available vehicles. Also offer transportation services for a fee.  |
| Passenger  |  A registered user who requests point-to-point transportation from a Renter who currently has an active vehicle booking. |
| Ride Request |  A request submitted by a passenger for a specific route and destination. |
| Listing | A vehicle entry created by an Owner with settings, schedule, and pricing. |
| Booking | A rental request submitted by a Renter for a specific vehicle. |
| Wear and Tear Charge | An additional per-hour charge set by the Owner to cover vehicle maintenance costs. |
| Max Renter Radius | The maximum distance in km that a Renter is allowed to take the vehicle from the pickup point. |
| Auto-accept | An Owner setting that automatically approves booking requests without manual review. |
| Saved Bike | A listing bookmarked by a Renter for easy future access. |

# **2\.  The Overall Description**

## **2.1 Product Perspective**

OurBike is a standalone web application targeting the university-town mobility gap. It is scoped specifically to motorized two-wheelers and to a context where the owner's idle window (time in class, time at work) is the availability window. OurBike uses time-only billing with a separate wear-and-tear component rather than distance or fuel metrics, reflecting the shorter trip distances typical of the target context.

The system consists of a browser-based frontend (React), a REST API backend (FastAPI), and a PostgreSQL database. The context diagram below shows the system's external actors and interfaces.

| \[ FIGURE: System Context Diagram \] |
| :---: |

## **2.2 Product Functions**

* Role based registration and login: users select Owner, Renter or both at signup and can toggle roles in app  
* Vehicle listing creation: Owners create listings with vehicle details, photos, pricing, schedule, and operating zone  
* Vehicle settings management: Owners configure availability toggle, auto-accept, hourly rate, wear-and-tear charge, schedule, and max renter radius  
* Vehicle browsing: Renters browse a grid of available bikes/scooters with photo, name, and hourly fare  
* Booking requests: Renters submit requests; Owner’s review (or auto-accept) and respond  
* Renters offering rides : Renters can browse available ride requests and accept them, transporting passengers to their destinations  
* Earnings tracking: Owners and Renters view available balance, earnings chart (1W/1M/3M/1Y), and per booking history with a Withdraw action  
* Passenger ride requests: Passengers can input a destination to request a ride from active Renters.  
* Ride fulfillment: Renters can browse nearby Passenger ride requests, accept them, and earn a flat fee for completing the trip.  
* Ratings: Owners see a history of Renter ratings per ride; Renters have a rating visible on their profile  
* Saved bikes: Renters can bookmark listings for quick future access


## **2.3 User Classes and Characteristics**

Two primary user classes interact with OurBike. A single account may hold both roles and switch between them using the role toggle in the application header.

### **2.3.1 Owner**

An Owner is a registered individual who possesses a motorized two-wheeler and wishes to earn from it during idle periods. Owners are expected to have basic digital literacy sufficient to complete a web form and manage a listing. They interact primarily with the vehicle settings screen, booking requests screen, earnings screen, and ratings screen.

Key characteristics presented in UI:

* Lists one or more vehicles with name, model, make, registration number, rate per hour, and photos

* Configures per vehicle settings: availability toggle, auto-accept bookings, hourly rate, wear and tear charge, available schedule, and max renter radius

* Accepts or rejects incoming booking requests (unless auto-accept is enabled)

* Monitors active vehicles, current fares, and pending requests from the dashboard

* Views total earnings, earnings chart and per booking revenue history

* Sees a history of ratings left by past Renters

### **2.3.2 Renter**

A Renter is a registered individual who needs short term access to a two-wheeler. Renters browse available vehicles, save favourites, submit booking requests and offer transportation for a fee . They are expected to be comfortable with mobile first booking style web apps like Pathao.

Key characteristics derived from UI:

* Browse a grid of available bikes/scooters showing vehicle photo, name, and fare per hour

* Can save/bookmark listings as Saved Bikes

* Submits booking requests for a specific vehicle

* Browse available ride requests and accept them

*  Transport passengers to their destinations for a fee

* Has a personal rating visible to Owners

* Views past trips count, saved bikes count, and rating from their dashboard

Note: The Administrator user class present in earlier drafts has been removed. No admin panel is implemented in this version.

### **2.3.3 Passenger**

A Passenger is a registered individual needing point-to-point transit. They interact with the search interface to find active Renters willing to offer rides.

Key characteristics derived from UI:  

* Inputs pickup and drop-off locations to find rides.  
* Views estimated fares, Renter ratings, and vehicle details before booking.  
* Submits ride requests and monitors their status.

## **2.4 Operating Environment**

* Browser based responsive web application; no native mobile app

* Supported browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge (latest versions)

* Minimum viewport: 375 px width (mobile)

* Frontend: React

* Backend: FastAPI

* Database: PostgreSQL

* Deployment: Cloud (provider TBD)

## **2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints**

* All functionality is browser based; no native mobile apps in scope

* Billing is time based only, no odometer input, no distance charge, no fuel charge in this version

* No real payment processing; earnings are tracked in the system but withdrawal is out of scope for the v0.1 UI flow

* GPS tracking is not implemented; the Owner sets a schedule and a max radius figure manually

* No license verification against an external authority

* No insurance measurement or damage deposit mechanism

## **2.6 Assumptions and Dependencies**

* Renters are assumed to possess a valid riding license; the system may store but does not verify it

* Renters are assumed to be responsible with the vehicle, e.g., taking photos before and after a ride

* Owners are assumed to maintain their vehicles in roadworthy condition; the platform bears no liability

* Both parties agree to a platform Terms of Service at registration

* \[Requirements in this document are grounded in unstructured interviews with prospective users. Survey results may revise requirements in a future version.

# **3\.  Specific Requirements**

**Convention:** "The system shall…" \= required. "The system should…" \= desired but deferrable. All requirements are uniquely numbered for traceability. Requirements are organized by user class per the IEEE 830 "organized by user class" outline.

##  **3.1 External Interfaces**

Wireframes are provided in Appendix D. Following demonstrates textual description of the interfaces.

| \# | Screen | User Class | Key Elements |
| ----- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Landing / Home | Any | Central search bar ("Where to?") for Renters/Passengers. Prominent "List a Vehicle" CTA for Owners. Bottom navigation bar (Search, Post/List, Inbox, Profile). |
| 2 | Search Results / Map | Renter / Passenger | Map view and horizontal list of available rides/vehicles. Cards feature vehicle photo, user avatar, rating, and fare. |
| 3 | Listing / Ride Details | Renter / Passenger | Full-screen detail view. Trust signals (Owner/Driver photo, verified badge, rating), exact pickup location, pricing breakdown, and a sticky "Book" button. |
| 4 | Create Listing | Owner | Step-by-step creation flow (Name, Model, Rate, Schedule, Photos) to reduce cognitive load. |
| 5 | Active Ride / Booking | All | Real-time status of the current ride/booking. Estimated time of arrival, current accumulated fare, and an "End Ride" or "Return Vehicle" action button. |
| 6 | Inbox / Requests | All | Visual cards for incoming/past requests. Features Passenger/Renter profile photo, route, and estimated fare before Accept/Reject buttons. |
| 7 | Profile & Dashboard | All | Consolidated view moved from the home screen. Contains status cards: Total Earnings (BDT), Past Trips, Saved Bikes, Rating score, and a 'Withdraw' placeholder button. |

Requirements are organized by user class. System functions are listed under 3.2.3.

### **3.2.1 Owner Functions**

### **3.2.1.1 Registration and Role Selection**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-AU-01 | Role Selection | The system shall present a landing screen asking the user whether they want to rent a bike or list their own, routing them to the appropriate registration or login flow. |
| FR-AU-02 | Owner Registration | The system shall allow a new Owner to register with full name, email address, phone numbER- and password. |
| FR-AU-03 | Login | The system shall authenticate registered users with email and password and issue a session token on success. |
| FR-AU-04 | Dual Role Toggle | The system shall allow a logged,in user to switch between Owner and Renter modes using a toggle in the application headER- without logging out. |

### **3.2.1.2 Vehicle Listing Creation**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-LM-01 | Create Listing | The system shall allow an Owner to create a vehicle listing by providing: vehicle name, model, make, registration numbER- rate per hour (BDT), and up to 5 photos. |
| FR-LM-02 | Add Scooter Action | The Owner Dashboard shall include an '+ Add scooter' button that navigates directly to the Create Listing screen. |
| FR-LM-03 | Listing Appears on Dashboard | After creation, the new vehicle shall appear in the Owner's vehicle list on the dashboard with an appropriate status label. |

### **3.2.1.3  Vehicle Settings**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-VS-01 | Availability Toggle | The system shall allow an Owner to toggle a vehicle as 'Available to rent', making it visible to Renters when on, and hiding it when off. |
| FR-VS-02 | Auto-accept Toggle | The system shall allow an Owner to enable 'Auto accept bookings', whereby incoming booking requests are automatically confirmed without manual Owner approval. |
| FR-VS-03 | Hourly Rate | The system shall allow an Owner to set an hourly rate (BDT) for a vehicle. This is the base price per hour of usage. |
| FR-VS-04 | Wear and Tear Charge | The system shall allow an Owner to set a wear,and,tear charge (BDT per hour) for a vehicle, charged in addition to the hourly rate to cover maintenance costs. |
| FR-VS-05 | Schedule | The system shall allow an Owner to define a recurring weekly schedule specifying the days and time window during which the vehicle is available for booking (e.g. Mon–Fri, 2–4 pm). |
| FR-VS-06 | Max Renter Radius | The system shall allow an Owner to set a maximum radius (km) representing how far a Renter may take the vehicle from the pickup point. |
| FR-VS-07 | Save Settings | The system shall persist all vehicle settings upon the Owner pressing 'Save settings'. Changes shall take effect immediately. |

### **3.2.1.4  Dashboard and Vehicle Status**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-OD-01 | Status Cards | The Owner Dashboard shall display summary cards showing: total scooters listed, number currently active (out on a ride), Owner's average rating, total earnings to date, and number of pending requests. |
| FR-OD-02 | Active Scooters List | The Owner Dashboard shall display a list of active (currently rented,out) vehicles showing vehicle photo, name, estimated return time, and current total fare. |
| FR-OD-03 | All Vehicles View | The system shall provide an 'All vehicles' view listing every vehicle the Owner has listed, with status (e.g. returning in X mins / in garage / last rented X hrs ago) and a 'See details' link. |
| FR-OD-04 | Vehicle Status Labels | Each vehicle in the Owner's list shall display one of the following statuses: actively rented (with return time and current fare), in garage currently not in use, or in garage with last rental timestamp. |

### **3.2.1.5  Booking Request Management**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-BK-01 | Requests Screen | The system shall provide a Requests screen with two tabs: 'Incoming requests' (with count) and 'Past requests' (with count). |
| FR-BK-02 | Request Card | Each incoming request card shall display: vehicle photo, vehicle name, renter name, pickup location, and estimated fare (BDT). |
| FR-BK-03 | Accept Request | The Owner shall be able to accept an incoming booking request. Acceptance confirms the booking and notifies the Renter. |
| FR-BK-04 | Reject Request | The Owner shall be able to reject an incoming booking request. Rejection notifies the Renter and returns the time slot to available. |
| FR-BK-05 | Auto-accept Bypass | When the vehicle's Auto-accept setting is enabled, incoming requests shall be automatically accepted without Owner action, and shall not appear in the Incoming requests list. |

| :---- | :---- | :---- |

| FR-ER-02 | Withdraw Action | The Earnings screen shall include a 'Withdraw' button. Actual fund transfer is out of scope for v0.1; the button shall be present as a placeholder. |
| FR-ER-03 | Earnings Chart | The Earnings screen shall display a bar chart of earnings for the selected period. Period options: 1 Week (1W), 1 Month (1M), 3 Months (3M), 1 Year (1Y). |
| FR-ER-04 | Recent Earnings List | The Earnings screen shall list recent individual earning entries showing: scooter name, renter name, time used, and amount earned (BDT). |

| :---- | :---- | :---- |

| FR-RT-03 | See Ride Details | Each rating entry shall include a 'See ride details' link navigating to the booking detail for that session. |
| FR-RT-04 | Owner Rating Score | The Owner's average rating shall be displayed as a summary card on the Owner Dashboard. |

| :---- | :---- | :---- |

| FR-RN-02 | Renter Dashboard | The system shall display a Renter Dashboard with status cards: Past trips (count), Saved bikes (count), Rating, and Total Earnings. |
| FR-RN-03 | Look for a Bike CTA | The Renter Dashboard shall include a 'Look for a bike' button that navigates to the Available Bikes / Search Results screen. |

### **3.2.2.2  Vehicle Discovery**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-VD-01 | Available Bikes Grid | The system shall display available vehicles in a grid of cards. Each card shall show: vehicle photo, vehicle name (make/model), fare per hour (BDT), and a 'See details' link. |
| FR-VD-02 | See Details | Selecting 'See details' on a listing card shall navigate to a listing detail view (content to be specified in a future revision once the detail screen wireframe is available). |
| FR-VD-03 | Save Bike | The system shall allow a Renter to save a listing as a Saved Bike. Saved count is reflected on the Renter Dashboard. |

### **3.2.2.3  Booking**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-BK-06 | Submit Booking Request | A Renter shall be able to submit a booking request for an available vehicle. |
| FR-BK-07 | Estimated Fare on Request | The system shall display an estimated fare (BDT) to the Owner on the incoming request card, calculated as: (hourly rate \+ wear and tear charge) × estimated duration. |
| FR-BK-08 | Renter Notification | The system shall notify the Renter when their booking request is accepted or rejected by the Owner. |

### **3.2.2.4  Renter Rating**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-RT-05 | Renter Rating Score | Each Renter shall have a personal rating score, visible to Owners on the booking request card and displayed on the Renter Dashboard. |
| FR-RT-06 | Rating After Ride | The system should allow an Owner to rate a Renter after a completed booking. The exact rating flow is to be specified in a future revision. |

### **3.2.3  System Functions**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-BI-01 | Billing Calculation | The system shall calculate the total fare for a completed booking as: total\_fare \= (hourly\_rate \+ wear\_and\_tear\_charge) × duration\_hours. Duration is computed from booking start to booking end time. |
| FR-BI-02 | Estimated Fare Display | The system shall display an estimated fare during a booking request based on the expected duration, hourly rate, and wear and tear charge of the selected vehicle. |
| FR-SY-01 | Role Toggle Persistence | The system shall remember the user's last active role (Owner / Renter) and default to it on next login. |
| FR-SY-02 | Status Transitions | The system shall automatically update vehicle and booking status (e.g. marking a vehicle as active when a booking starts, returning it to available when a booking ends). |

## **3.3  Performance Requirements**

* NFR-P-01: The Available Bikes grid shall load within 2 seconds under normal load (up to 50 concurrent users).

* NFR-P-02: Any primary screen shall fully load within 3 seconds on a standard broadband connection.

* NFR-P-03: Billing calculation shall complete within 1 second of booking end confirmation.

## **3.4  Logical Database Requirements**

The following entities and relationships form the logical data model of OurBike. The class diagram in Appendix A provides the full visual representation.

| Entity | Key Attributes | Relationships |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| User | id, name, email, passwordHash, phone, roles\[\] | 1 User → 0..\* Listings (as Owner); 1 User → 0..\* Bookings (as Renter) |
| Listing | id, ownerId, vehicleName, model, make, regNumbER- hourlyRate, wearTearRate, isAvailable, autoAccept, scheduleDays, scheduleStaRT- scheduleEnd, maxRadiusKm, photos\[\] | 1 Listing → 0..\* Bookings; belongs to 1 User (Owner) |
| Booking | id, listingId, renterId, status, estimatedFare, startTime, endTime, totalFare, pickupLocation | 1 Booking → 1 Bill (on completion); belongs to 1 Listing and 1 User (Renter) |
| Bill | id, bookingId, durationHours, hourlyRate, wearTearRate, totalFare | Belongs to 1 Booking |
| Rating | id, bookingId, raterId, rateeId, score (1–5) | Belongs to 1 Booking; links two Users |
| SavedBike | id, renterId, listingId, savedAt | Links 1 User (Renter) to 1 Listing |
| PassengerTrip | id, passengerId, renterId, bookingId, pickupLoc, dropoffLoc, fare, status | Belongs to 1 User (Passenger) and 1 User (Renter). Links to 1 active Booking. (Add this to Integrity constraints) A PassengerTrip can only be created if the renterId has an Active Booking status for a Listing. |

Integrity constraints:

* A Booking may not overlap with another active Booking for the same Listing.

* A Bill is created once per Booking on transition to Complete status.

* A Listing may not be deleted while a Booking is in Pending or Active status.

* A Rating record links to exactly one Booking and may be created only once per party per Booking.

## **3.5  Design Constraints**

* The system shall be implemented as a browser-based web application (React \+ FastAPI \+ PostgreSQL) deployable on a cloud server.

* All source code shall be version controlled in a Git repository.

* No secret credentials shall be hard coded; all secrets shall be stored as environment variables.

* Billing shall be time based only in this version; no distance or fuel fields shall appear in the UI.

### **3.5.1  Standards Compliance**

* This SRS conforms to IEEE Std 830,1998.

* Password storage shall follow OWASP guidelines (bcrypt).

* All user-facing monetary values shall be displayed in BDT.

## **3.6  Software System Attributes**

### **3.6.1  Reliability**

The system shall not lose any completed Booking or Bill record in the event of an unexpected crash. In-progress booking timing data may be recalculated from stored start times on restart.

### **3.6.2  Availability**

The system shall target 99% uptime during the academic submission and demonstration period.

### **3.6.3  Security**

* NFR-S-01: Passwords shall be stored as salted hashes (bcrypt or equivalent).

* NFR-S-02: All HTTP traffic shall be served over HTTPS.

* NFR-S-03: Session tokens shall expire after 7 days of inactivity.

* NFR-S-04: All user inputs shall be sanitized server-side to prevent SQL injection and XSS.

* NFR-S-05: Owner only endpoints (vehicle settings, earnings, ratings) shall reject requests from Renter-only sessions with HTTP 403\.

### **3.6.4  Maintainability**

* NFR-M-01: Frontend and backend shall be in clearly separated modules.

* NFR-M-02: REST API endpoints shall follow RESTful naming conventions and be documented in a README.

* NFR-M-03: Database schema changes shall be managed through versioned migration scripts.

### **3.6.5  Portability**

* The application shall run on any Linux server with a compatible Python and Node.js runtime.

* No platform specific (Windows/macOS) APIs shall be used.

# **4\.  External Interface Requirements**

## **4.1  User Interface**

The UI is organized around a role toggle in the header that switches between Owner and Renter views. The green colour scheme and card layout are consistent across all Owner screens; the blue colour scheme is used for Renter-facing screens (visible in Available Bikes grid). All screens are designed mobile first.

## **4.2  Software Interfaces**

* Transactional Email: the system shall send notification emails (booking request received, booking accepted/rejected). A sandbox provider (e.g., Resend) shall be used in development.

* PostgreSQL: all persistent data stored in a relational PostgreSQL database, accessed via SQLAlchemy ORM from the FastAPI backend.

* File/Object Storage: vehicle listing photos stored in a server accessible directory or S3 compatible bucket.

## **4.3  Communications Interfaces**

* All client-server communication shall use HTTPS with JSON payloads.

* Real-time booking status updates (Owner dashboard active vehicle status, fare accumulation) shall be implemented via WebSocket or HTTP polling, to be decided during design.

# **5\.  Change Management Process**

* All change requests shall be submitted in writing (email or shared document) to both authors, including the affected requirement ID, the proposed change, and the rationale.

* The team shall evaluate and respond within 3 business days: Accepted, Rejected, or Deferred.

* Accepted changes trigger a new version number and a new Revision History row.

* The course instructor shall be notified of scope affecting changes.

# **1\.  Introduction**

## **1.1 Purpose**

This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) defines the functional and non-functional requirements for OurBike, a peer-to-peer motorized two-wheeler rental web application. It is intended for use by the development team and course instructors. This document follows the IEEE Std 830-1998 standard.

## **1.2 Scope**

**Product name:** OurBike.

OurBike is a web-based platform that enables owners of motorcycles and scooters to list their vehicles for short-term rental during periods of non-use. For example, while the owner is in class or at work. Renters can browse available vehicles, send a booking request, and are billed by the hour. The Owner sets an hourly rate and a wear-and-tear charge per hour; the total fare is calculated from the actual time used.

**The system will:** 

* Allow vehicle owners to list, configure, and activate their two-wheelers for rental

* Allow renters to browse available vehicles and send booking requests

* Compute billing based on time used, hourly rate, and wear-and-tear charge

* Provide owners with earnings tracking and booking management

* Support a rating system for renters

**The system will not (in this version):** 

* Process real financial transactions. Billing is tracked but payment is handled outside the platform

* Perform live GPS tracking or automatic odometer reading

* Include distance-based or fuel-based billing

* Provide a native mobile application. All functionality is browser-based

* Include an administrator moderation panel

## **1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations**

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| Owner | A registered user who lists one or more vehicles for rental. |
| Renter | A registered user who browses and books available vehicles. |
| Listing | A vehicle entry created by an Owner with settings, schedule, and pricing. |
| Booking | A rental request submitted by a Renter for a specific vehicle. |
| Wear and Tear Charge | An additional per-hour charge set by the Owner to cover vehicle maintenance costs. |
| Max Renter Radius | The maximum distance in km that a Renter is allowed to take the vehicle from the pickup point. |
| Auto-accept | An Owner setting that automatically approves booking requests without manual review. |
| Saved Bike | A listing bookmarked by a Renter for easy future access. |
| SRS | Software Requirements Specification |
| FR | Functional Requirement |
| NFR | Non-Functional Requirement |
| BDT | Bangladeshi Taka , the currency used throughout the platform |
| UI | User Interface |
| API | Application Programming Interface |

Section 4 specifies external interface requirements. Appendices provide the user class diagram, sequence diagram, booking state diagram, and UI wireframe references.

# **2\.  The Overall Description**

## **2.1 Product Perspective**

OurBike is a standalone web application targeting the university-town mobility gap. It is scoped specifically to motorized two-wheelers and to a context where the owner's idle window (time in class, time at work) is the availability window. OurBike uses time-only billing with a separate wear-and-tear component rather than distance or fuel metrics, reflecting the shorter trip distances typical of the target context.

The system consists of a browser-based frontend (React), a REST API backend (FastAPI), and a PostgreSQL database. The context diagram below shows the system's external actors and interfaces.

| \[ FIGURE: System Context Diagram \] |
| :---: |

## **2.2 Product Functions**

* Role based registration and login: users select Owner, Renter or both at signup and can toggle roles in app

* Vehicle listing creation: Owners create listings with vehicle details, photos, pricing, schedule, and operating zone

* Vehicle settings management: Owners configure availability toggle, auto-accept, hourly rate, wear-and-tear charge, schedule, and max renter radius

* Vehicle browsing: Renters browse a grid of available bikes/scooters with photo, name, and hourly fare

* Booking requests: Renters submit requests; Owner’s review (or auto-accept) and respond

* Earnings tracking: Owners view available balance, earnings chart (1W/1M/3M/1Y), and per booking history with a Withdraw action

* Ratings: Owners see a history of Renter ratings per ride; Renters have a rating visible on their profile

* Saved bikes: Renters can bookmark listings for quick future access

## **2.3 User Classes and Characteristics**

Two primary user classes interact with OurBike. A single account may hold both roles and switch between them using the role toggle in the application header.

### **2.3.1 Owner**

An Owner is a registered individual who possesses a motorized two-wheeler and wishes to earn from it during idle periods. Owners are expected to have basic digital literacy sufficient to complete a web form and manage a listing. They interact primarily with the vehicle settings screen, booking requests screen, earnings screen, and ratings screen.

Key characteristics presented in UI:

* Lists one or more vehicles with name, model, make, registration number, rate per hour, and photos

* Configures per vehicle settings: availability toggle, auto-accept bookings, hourly rate, wear and tear charge, available schedule, and max renter radius

* Accepts or rejects incoming booking requests (unless auto-accept is enabled)

* Monitors active vehicles, current fares, and pending requests from the dashboard

* Views total earnings, earnings chart and per booking revenue history

* Sees a history of ratings left by past Renters

### **2.3.2 Renter**

A Renter is a registered individual who needs short term access to a two-wheeler. Renters browse available vehicles, save favourites, and submit booking requests. They are expected to be comfortable with mobile first booking style web apps.

Key characteristics derived from UI:

* Browses a grid of available bikes/scooters showing vehicle photo, name, and fare per hour

* Can save/bookmark listings as Saved Bikes

* Submits booking requests for a specific vehicle

* Has a personal rating visible to Owners

* Views past trips count, saved bikes count, and rating from their dashboard

Note: The Administrator user class present in earlier drafts has been removed. No admin panel is implemented in this version.

## **2.4 Operating Environment**

* Browser based responsive web application; no native mobile app

* Supported browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge (latest versions)

* Minimum viewport: 375 px width (mobile)

* Frontend: React

* Backend: FastAPI

* Database: PostgreSQL

* Deployment: Cloud (provider TBD)

## **2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints**

* All functionality is browser based; no native mobile apps in scope

* Billing is time based only, no odometer input, no distance charge, no fuel charge in this version

* No real payment processing; earnings are tracked in the system but withdrawal is out of scope for the v0.1 UI flow

* GPS tracking is not implemented; the Owner sets a schedule and a max radius figure manually

* No license verification against an external authority

* No insurance measurement or damage deposit mechanism

## **2.6 Assumptions and Dependencies**

* Renters are assumed to possess a valid riding license; the system may store but does not verify it

* Renters are assumed to be responsible with the vehicle, e.g., taking photos before and after a ride

* Owners are assumed to maintain their vehicles in roadworthy condition; the platform bears no liability

* Both parties agree to a platform Terms of Service at registration

* \[Requirements in this document are grounded in unstructured interviews with prospective users. Survey results may revise requirements in a future version.

* Supporting academic literature on P2P vehicle sharing demand has been identified but not yet formally cited; references will be added in the next revision.\]

| FR-VS-03 | Hourly Rate | The system shall allow an Owner to set an hourly rate (BDT) for a vehicle. This is the base price per hour of usage. |
| FR-VS-04 | Wear and Tear Charge | The system shall allow an Owner to set a wear,and,tear charge (BDT per hour) for a vehicle, charged in addition to the hourly rate to cover maintenance costs. |
| FR-VS-05 | Schedule | The system shall allow an Owner to define a recurring weekly schedule specifying the days and time window during which the vehicle is available for booking (e.g. Mon–Fri, 2–4 pm). |

| FR-VS-07 | Save Settings | The system shall persist all vehicle settings upon the Owner pressing 'Save settings'. Changes shall take effect immediately. |

| FR-OD-04 | Vehicle Status Labels | Each vehicle in the Owner's list shall display one of the following statuses: actively rented (with return time and current fare), in garage currently not in use, or in garage with last rental timestamp. |

| FR-BK-02 | Request Card | Each incoming request card shall display: vehicle photo, vehicle name, renter name, pickup location, and estimated fare (BDT). |
| FR-BK-03 | Accept Request | The Owner shall be able to accept an incoming booking request. Acceptance confirms the booking and notifies the Renter. |
| FR-BK-04 | Reject Request | The Owner shall be able to reject an incoming booking request. Rejection notifies the Renter and returns the time slot to available. |
| FR-BK-05 | Auto-accept Bypass | When the vehicle's Auto-accept setting is enabled, incoming requests shall be automatically accepted without Owner action, and shall not appear in the Incoming requests list. |

| FR-RN-02 | Renter Dashboard | The system shall display a Renter Dashboard with status cards: Past trips (count), Saved bikes (count), Rating, and Total Earnings. |
| FR-RN-03 | Look for a Bike CTA | The Renter Dashboard shall include a 'Look for a bike' button that navigates to the Available Bikes / Search Results screen. |

### **3.2.2.2  Vehicle Discovery**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-VD-01 | Available Bikes Grid | The system shall display available vehicles in a grid of cards. Each card shall show: vehicle photo, vehicle name (make/model), fare per hour (BDT), and a 'See details' link. |
| FR-VD-02 | See Details | Selecting 'See details' on a listing card shall navigate to a listing detail view (content to be specified in a future revision once the detail screen wireframe is available). |

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-BK-06 | Submit Booking Request | A Renter shall be able to submit a booking request for an available vehicle. |
| FR-BK-07 | Estimated Fare on Request | The system shall display an estimated fare (BDT) to the Owner on the incoming request card, calculated as: (hourly rate \+ wear and tear charge) × estimated duration. |
| FR-BK-08 | Renter Notification | The system shall notify the Renter when their booking request is accepted or rejected by the Owner. |

### **3.2.2.4  Renter Rating**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-RT-05 | Renter Rating Score | Each Renter shall have a personal rating score, visible to Owners on the booking request card and displayed on the Renter Dashboard. |

### **3.2.3  System Functions**

| ID | Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-BI-01 | Billing Calculation | The system shall calculate the total fare for a completed booking as: total\_fare \= (hourly\_rate \+ wear\_and\_tear\_charge) × duration\_hours. Duration is computed from booking start to booking end time. |
| FR-BI-02 | Estimated Fare Display | The system shall display an estimated fare during a booking request based on the expected duration, hourly rate, and wear and tear charge of the selected vehicle. |
| FR-SY-01 | Role Toggle Persistence | The system shall remember the user's last active role (Owner / Renter) and default to it on next login. |
| FR-SY-02 | Status Transitions | The system shall automatically update vehicle and booking status (e.g. marking a vehicle as active when a booking starts, returning it to available when a booking ends). |

## **3.3  Performance Requirements**

* NFR-P-01: The Available Bikes grid shall load within 2 seconds under normal load (up to 50 concurrent users).

* NFR-P-02: Any primary screen shall fully load within 3 seconds on a standard broadband connection.

* NFR-P-03: Billing calculation shall complete within 1 second of booking end confirmation.

## **3.4  Logical Database Requirements**

The following entities and relationships form the logical data model of OurBike. The class diagram in Appendix A provides the full visual representation.

| Entity | Key Attributes | Relationships |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| User | id, name, email, passwordHash, phone, roles\[\] | 1 User → 0..\* Listings (as Owner); 1 User → 0..\* Bookings (as Renter) |
| Listing | id, ownerId, vehicleName, model, make, regNumbER- hourlyRate, wearTearRate, isAvailable, autoAccept, scheduleDays, scheduleStaRT- scheduleEnd, maxRadiusKm, photos\[\] | 1 Listing → 0..\* Bookings; belongs to 1 User (Owner) |
| Booking | id, listingId, renterId, status, estimatedFare, startTime, endTime, totalFare, pickupLocation | 1 Booking → 1 Bill (on completion); belongs to 1 Listing and 1 User (Renter) |
| Bill | id, bookingId, durationHours, hourlyRate, wearTearRate, totalFare | Belongs to 1 Booking |
| Rating | id, bookingId, raterId, rateeId, score (1–5) | Belongs to 1 Booking; links two Users |
| SavedBike | id, renterId, listingId, savedAt | Links 1 User (Renter) to 1 Listing |

Integrity constraints:

* A Booking may not overlap with another active Booking for the same Listing.

* A Bill is created once per Booking on transition to Complete status.

* A Listing may not be deleted while a Booking is in Pending or Active status.

* A Rating record links to exactly one Booking and may be created only once per party per Booking.

## **3.5  Design Constraints**

* The system shall be implemented as a browser-based web application (React \+ FastAPI \+ PostgreSQL) deployable on a cloud server.

* All source code shall be version controlled in a Git repository.

* No secret credentials shall be hard coded; all secrets shall be stored as environment variables.

* Billing shall be time based only in this version; no distance or fuel fields shall appear in the UI.

### **3.5.1  Standards Compliance**

* This SRS conforms to IEEE Std 830,1998.

* Password storage shall follow OWASP guidelines (bcrypt).

* All user-facing monetary values shall be displayed in BDT.

## **3.6  Software System Attributes**

### **3.6.1  Reliability**

The system shall not lose any completed Booking or Bill record in the event of an unexpected crash. In-progress booking timing data may be recalculated from stored start times on restart.

### **3.6.2  Availability**

The system shall target 99% uptime during the academic submission and demonstration period.

### **3.6.3  Security**

* NFR-S-01: Passwords shall be stored as salted hashes (bcrypt or equivalent).

* NFR-S-02: All HTTP traffic shall be served over HTTPS.

* NFR-S-03: Session tokens shall expire after 7 days of inactivity.

* NFR-S-04: All user inputs shall be sanitized server-side to prevent SQL injection and XSS.

* NFR-S-05: Owner only endpoints (vehicle settings, earnings, ratings) shall reject requests from Renter-only sessions with HTTP 403\.

### **3.6.4  Maintainability**

* NFR-M-01: Frontend and backend shall be in clearly separated modules.

* NFR-M-02: REST API endpoints shall follow RESTful naming conventions and be documented in a README.

* NFR-M-03: Database schema changes shall be managed through versioned migration scripts.

### **3.6.5  Portability**

* The application shall run on any Linux server with a compatible Python and Node.js runtime.

* No platform specific (Windows/macOS) APIs shall be used.

# **4\.  External Interface Requirements**

## **4.1  User Interface**

The UI is organized around a role toggle in the header that switches between Owner and Renter views. The green colour scheme and card layout are consistent across all Owner screens; the blue colour scheme is used for Renter-facing screens (visible in Available Bikes grid). All screens are designed mobile first.

## **4.2  Software Interfaces**

* Transactional Email: the system shall send notification emails (booking request received, booking accepted/rejected). A sandbox provider (e.g., Resend) shall be used in development.

* PostgreSQL: all persistent data stored in a relational PostgreSQL database, accessed via SQLAlchemy ORM from the FastAPI backend.

* File/Object Storage: vehicle listing photos stored in a server accessible directory or S3 compatible bucket.

## **4.3  Communications Interfaces**

* All client-server communication shall use HTTPS with JSON payloads.

* Real-time booking status updates (Owner dashboard active vehicle status, fare accumulation) shall be implemented via WebSocket or HTTP polling, to be decided during design.

# **5\.  Change Management Process**

* All change requests shall be submitted in writing (email or shared document) to both authors, including the affected requirement ID, the proposed change, and the rationale.

* The team shall evaluate and respond within 3 business days: Accepted, Rejected, or Deferred.

* Accepted changes trigger a new version number and a new Revision History row.

* The course instructor shall be notified of scope affecting changes.

# Tab 2

# **1\. Idea Description**

OurBike is a web-based, peer-to-peer (P2P) rental platform designed specifically for motorized two-wheelers (scooters and motorcycles) within university campuses and urban micro-mobility hubs. It enables vehicle owners to monetise their two-wheelers during idle periods—such as while attending classes or working—by renting them out to peers on a flexible, hourly basis.

# **2\. Main Stakeholders**

**Vehicle Owners**: University students, faculty, or staff who own scooters/motorcycles that sit unused for extended hours throughout the day.

**Renters**: Students or local commuters needing affordable, short-distance, on-demand transportation without the capital or maintenance overhead of owning a vehicle.

**Platform Administrators/Instructors**: Academic and technical overseers monitoring system deployment, performance metrics, and operational compliance.

# **3\. Real-World Problem**

University campuses and urban dense zones face significant micro-mobility challenges:

**Idle Asset Inefficiency**: Motorcycles and scooters sit idle in parking lots for 6–8 hours daily, losing value while occupying limited parking space.

**First-Mile/Last-Mile Mobility Defici**t: Students frequently face long walks between campus buildings, libraries, or nearby transit hubs, while public transit and ride-hailing services are often costly or inflexible for short intra-campus trips.

**High Ownership Costs**: Purchasing and maintaining a private vehicle is financially unfeasible for many students.

# **4\. Proposed Solution, Effectiveness & Key Merits**

## **Proposed Solution**

OurBike bridges the gap with a localized, time-based P2P rental platform. Owners configure vehicle availability schedules, custom hourly rates, and a dedicated wear-and-tear maintenance fee. Renters browse nearby listings via a mobile-responsive web app, bookmark preferred rides, and submit hourly rental requests with instant auto-approval capabilities.

## **Effectiveness & Merits**

**Hyper-Localized Asset Utilization**: Shared micro-mobility platforms significantly reduce urban traffic congestion and vehicle idle time. Research by the Transportation Research Board (TRB) indicates that shared P2P vehicle initiatives can increase asset utilization by up to 40%–60%, turning static parking lots into active mobility nodes.  
Dual-Value Economic Model: Owners offset vehicle maintenance and fuel expenses through automated earning trackers, while renters access transportation at a fraction of standard ride-hailing costs.

**Fair Transparent Pricing**: By coupling an hourly base fare with a dedicated wear-and-tear charge (in BDT), the pricing model explicitly accounts for vehicular depreciation without requiring complex odometer hardware or live GPS integrations.  
Low Friction & High Accessibility: Built on a responsive web stack (React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL), OurBike eliminates app-store download barriers, ensuring universal accessibility across desktop and mobile browsers.
